title: A certified intercept preserves the original nonsmooth target and count
statement: For convex G-Lipschitz observation,Moreau envelope acquires a proposal only;rejection uses a supporting plane of ORIGINAL loss. Exact-support floors are exp[-G sqrt(V_o)-9/4] and,with negative quadratic block,exp[-V_minus/2-G sqrt(V_o)-11/4]. These are NOT implemented finite-polyhedral floors. Actual rational affine-piece/dual-gap/projected-gradient/simplex completion uses conservative exp[-G sqrt(V_o)-9/2] and exp[-V_minus/2-G sqrt(V_o)-6]. Approximate planes need certified intercept correction. For original minorant ell(y)=v dot y+c,count logZ_phi=psi(-v)-c+logA; joint negative block gives psi(-a_minus,-v)+||a_minus||^2/2-c+logA. Using the envelope tangent intercept can give wrong count even if accepted samples are correct. Smoothing target itself changed a reported posterior by TV~.1186. Curvature/information/fluctuation and finite-bit budgets still cost;no cheap arbitrary hard constraints.
